paragraph: Dasaratha's voice was deep and sonorous like that of a giant gong. It rang across the hall with a booming resonance as he said, 'Sixty thousand years have I lived under the royal canopy. Born of the Ikshvaku dynasty, treading the noble path of my ancestors, I have protected and ruled my people to the best of my ability, endeavoring eternally to establish dharma on this earth. With the permission of all the eminent sages and Brahmins, I seek repose due to my ageing body and failing strength. I desire to install Rama, who is as mighty as Indra and my equal in virtue, as king. I ask your approval to crown him the very next morrow.' Amidst thunderous noises of happy acceptance the distinguished dignitaries said that it was their cherished wish to see Rama as king. Dasaratha asked, "Your haste in accepting my proposal raises doubts about myself. Have I erred? Where have I gone wrong?" To the king's query, the monarchs and the other assembled said, "Divine one, the qualities and glory of Rama, surpass those of all other Ikshvaku. He is the noblest. Rooted in truth, versed in every branch of knowledge, he knows neither jealousy nor envy. His charming disposition makes him easily accessible. Receiving all with goodwill and grace, his compassion is so profound that with a single glance he can delve into the hearts of men. Innumerable and rare are the attributes of Rama. Mounted on horse, elephant or chariot, he never fails to enquire of the welfare of all those that come his way. Each utterance is accompanied by a sweet smile. Like a father and like a friend does he endear himself to his subjects, who adore and worship him. Handsome, as Lord Visnu, he is capable of ruling all the worlds and is the God of gods. To your good fortune and for the welfare of the world Rama is born as your son and is worshipped by the devatas. The world prays and invokes all that is divine for the prosperity and protection of him who never deviates from the path of dharma. He has every virtue. A virtue not possessed by him does not exist in this world. Without delay enthrone Rama as king" was the unanimous opinion of the people of the land.
Chapter/Canto/Verse_Reference: Ayodhya Kanda, Sarga 2 (Dasaratha's Proposal and Public Acclaim for Rama)
Situation/Problem_Faced: King Dasaratha, after ruling for sixty thousand years, feels the effects of old age and failing strength. He wishes to abdicate his throne and install his virtuous son, Rama, as the next king. He seeks the approval and consent of the assembled sages, Brahmins, monarchs, and other dignitaries for this decision.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: This passage highlights the concept of ideal kingship and the qualities of an exemplary ruler. Dasaratha demonstrates prudent governance by seeking counsel and approval for such a significant decision. The unanimous endorsement of Rama by the assembly underscores Rama's virtues and universal appeal, emphasizing qualities like truthfulness, compassion, humility, knowledge, and adherence to Dharma as essential for a king. It also shows the importance of a ruler's connection with and adoration by his subjects.
Outcome/Resolution: Dasaratha proposes Rama's coronation, and the assembled dignitaries and people enthusiastically and unanimously approve. Their response is overwhelmingly positive, praising Rama's unparalleled virtues and confirming his suitability for kingship. This sets the stage for Rama's proposed coronation, demonstrating widespread support for Dasaratha's choice.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Tyaga (Renunciation/Sacrifice - in Dasaratha's case, giving up the throne)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: King Dasaratha, embodying Rajya Dharma after millennia of righteous rule, proposes to abdicate due to age, seeking to install his supremely virtuous son, Rama, as the next king. The overwhelming, unanimous spiritual affirmation of Rama by all present, who laud his adherence to Dharma and countless Gunas, underscores his divine qualities and fitness for leadership. This spiritual consensus highlights the importance of a ruler's alignment with divine principles for the welfare of the world.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Psychologically, this passage showcases Dasaratha's exemplary leadership in managing a crucial succession planning phase with humility, even experiencing brief anxiety about his decision. Rama's character, defined by his profound integrity, emotional regulation (no jealousy or envy), and compassionate approach, inspires universal public approval and adoration. The scene demonstrates the profound psychological impact of a leader's virtues on the collective consciousness, fostering trust and a sense of well-being among the populace.
